quick.topic: Say how fresh the data is
quick.summary: Why a correct dashboard gets called wrong, and the one line that prevents it.
quick.takeaway: Say when the data was last updated, in their terms.

parts.title: Say how fresh the data is

beats.line: Sales said my dashboard is wrong. It shows no orders from this morning. Is it broken?

board.text: Say how fresh the data is

beats.line: Once a night. So this morning is not in yet.
Then it is correct, and still looks wrong to them.
Put the freshness where they look. Updated at what time.
Should I explain the nightly batch job to them?
No. They need the meaning, not the machinery.
Say what it means for their question.
This shows orders up to last night. Today’s appear tomorrow morning.
Now it reads as a limit, not a bug.

quiz.question: A business user says a nightly dashboard is wrong because today’s orders are missing. What is the best reply?
options: It shows orders up to last night; today’s appear tomorrow morning.
The batch job runs on a schedule at two.
quiz.explanation: It explains the limit in terms of their question, without the machinery behind it.

quiz.question: Showing when data was last updated helps people trust a dashboard.
quiz.explanation: People can see a missing morning is a timing limit, not an error.
